feature: Repair dirty integration rollback, stale integrated plans, arbitration retries, and generic commit failure loops.
global_constraints: All artifacts, test names, comments, diagnostics, and documentation are English-only.
No new production dependencies, provider calls in tests, or changes to model selection.
Preserve public CLI arguments and existing successful execution paths; mechanical failures must propagate nonzero exit codes.
Preserve append-only ledger history through ledger-append, including its per-task partitions; never rewrite old events to manufacture progress.
Never stash, discard, clean, force-remove, or commit user changes as a recovery mechanism.
Keep changes limited to the four findings and their regression coverage and documentation.
touches contains implementation and documentation paths only; author new test files outside touches, as required by brief-scaffold and keep-discard.
Existing committed tests remain unchanged; add regression modules and reuse their fixture conventions without weakening existing assertions.
Keep Bash/Git Bash and native Python path compatibility, including repository paths containing spaces.
The executor records real RED evidence before implementing each behavior and runs the authoritative gates afterward.
Read spec sections 5 and 6 for validation and self-host bootstrap: use explicit Python/Bash gates, real machine-readable RED evidence, and a validated external controller or task-by-task execution.
Use scripts/cmd for LLM-facing commands; retain full reports. Workers do not commit under Script CEO. This handoff does not authorize publication, pushing, or PR creation.

tasks.title: Reject dirty integration checkouts before mutation
tasks.summary: Add a fail-closed entry guard to integrate so batch rollback cannot delete pre-existing edits. Author test_integrate_dirty_guard.py in skills/two-model-sdd-pipeline/tests using disposable Git repositories and gate stubs.
acceptance: Staged changes, unstaged tracked edits, or non-ignored untracked files cause integrate to exit 1 before merging, resetting, releasing, or recording success, on both single-task and batch paths including approved no-op branches.

A rejected call preserves HEAD, staged blobs, tracked and untracked file bytes, task branches, and task worktrees; stderr identifies the dirty checkout and each requested task receives an integration_failed event with that reason.
A failed git status command blocks integration instead of treating absent output as a clean checkout.
Ignored pipeline artifacts alone do not block integration, and a clean batch whose gate fails still uses the existing fallback without losing independently valid sibling tasks.
The new regression module demonstrates the original data loss or missing guard in RED and passes after the fix; existing integration/worktree tests remain unchanged and pass.

tasks.title: Refresh and validate the plan after integration
tasks.summary: Keep the integration workspace snapshot synchronized with the tracked plan after normal, partial, and recovery integration. Author test_plan_refresh_after_integration.py in skills/two-model-sdd-pipeline/tests and exercise real scheduling after a merged plan edit.
acceptance: After every integration attempt that may change HEAD, refresh the plan before failed-task membership, task counts, the next wave, or final-review decisions; cover partial nonzero results and successful recovery integration.

When a task merges a tracked plan containing a new incomplete task, the next wave schedules that task and does not emit FINAL_REVIEW; merged dependency and acceptance changes also appear in the refreshed snapshot.

Snapshot replacement validates the minimum schema in spec section 3.2 and is atomic; missing, unreadable, malformed, duplicate-ID, or unusable plans block without destroying the previous snapshot or proceeding on stale data.
Refresh preserves ledger history and partitions, session records, briefs, and reports; source-equals-destination and paths containing spaces work.
With TOTAL omitted, task counts follow the refreshed plan; an explicit TOTAL differing from the current count blocks before task advancement or closing, including serial execution.
The new regression module fails against stale-plan behavior and passes after the fix; existing scheduler, workspace, and run-pipeline behavior remains compatible.

tasks.title: Start a new execution attempt after arbitration
tasks.summary: Use the latest successful arbitration resolution as the boundary for incomplete-task routing, and resume the correct coder with the refreshed brief before evaluating gates. Author test_arbitration_execution_retry.py in skills/two-model-sdd-pipeline/tests with realistic dispatch events and preserved historical ledgers.
acceptance: Append arbitrate_resolved only after director success and successful plan refresh; a refresh failure blocks without claiming the ruling is ready for execution.
An incomplete task routes BRIEF then RED after resolution, ignoring pre-resolution red_check, commit, and review state for current-attempt progress; completed tasks keep their terminal behavior.
Before the new dispatch, archive active coder/reviewer logs, parsed review, and RED evidence without overwriting an existing attempt archive or removing per-agent session records.

The toolchain-selected coder receives the corrected brief and resumes its own session when available, otherwise starts fresh; no reviewer session is used for coder execution and Flutter continues through the existing delegating shim.

Both TEST_DEFECT before commit and review ESCALATE after commit can reach a fresh gate, fresh reviewer result, and approval without replaying old failures; stale RED evidence and old verdicts cannot satisfy the new attempt.
An interrupted dispatch propagates its error without entering coder-gate; a genuine subsequent escalation remains a bounded blocker, not an unbounded director loop.
The regression module covers global-only and partitioned histories, preserved implementation work and archives, successful retry, interrupted retry, and genuine repeated escalation.

tasks.title: Block explicitly on empty or failed generic commits
tasks.summary: Separate test success from commit success in the generic coder gate and preserve actionable Git diagnostics. Author test_coder_commit_outcomes.py in skills/two-model-sdd-pipeline/tests, including a task-run check proving commit failures terminate rather than cycle.
acceptance: A generic gate with valid RED evidence and green tests but no staged changes exits 1 with an explicit empty-commit blocker, without reviewer dispatch or a commit/task_complete event.
Staging errors, staged-diff inspection errors, and real commit failures exit 1 with useful diagnostics and preserve the working tree/index rather than reporting nothing to commit.
Git diff exit status for changed content is distinguished from a command error; successful staging and commits retain their normal commit event, review-package generation, and reviewer dispatch.
Neither empty nor failed commits are converted to TEST_DEFECT, an automatic empty commit, or task approval.
The real orchestrator/task-run path stops on failed or empty commits without repeating gates or provider calls; any coder_round PASS records only gate success and does not mask the nonzero return.
The new module covers clean-tree, failed-hook, staging-error, inspection-error, and successful-commit cases; existing generic and Flutter gate tests remain compatible.

tasks.title: Verify composed recovery and document the corrected contracts
tasks.summary: Author test_recovery_hardening_e2e.py in skills/two-model-sdd-pipeline/tests to verify the composed fixes with real routing, refresh, ledger propagation, and disposable Git integration. Update human and agent documentation to match the implemented blockers and recovery progression.
acceptance: A composed scenario arbitrates a task, incorporates a director-added later task, obtains fresh coder/reviewer approval, integrates and refreshes the plan, and executes the added task before closing.
Composed dirty-integration and generic-commit-failure scenarios stop before closing without losing edits or entering retry loops; provider calls remain stubbed and bounded by test timeouts.

README.txt, README-LLM.md, and CONTEXT.md accurately document dirty-tree rejection, tracked-plan refresh, arbitration attempt boundaries/session reuse, and explicit generic commit blockers without promising automatic no-op approval.

Both complete Python unittest suites listed in spec section 5 pass, targeted shell lint and syntax checks pass, and git diff --check passes; environment or pre-existing failures are reported separately and are never hidden by weakening checks.

The final committed checkpoint passes doc-check, the four original reproduction scenarios are covered, and the handoff report records verification evidence and any residual limitations without publishing or pushing.
